title: What implements sandboxed execution, and which tier first?
statement: REQ-0005 requires claims to be testable by execution in a real environment. #56 decides three tiers and #77 decides how they activate, but no controller exists for any of them. Which tier is built first, and what provisions, executes, observes and destroys?
notes: BLOCKING under DEC-0002. BOUNDARIES BEFORE MECHANISM (DEC-0003): (a) what may execute — which claims justify running code at all; (b) filesystem, network and credential boundaries per tier (#56), and what a tier may NOT reach; (c) resource limits — time, cost, instance count — since #77's authorisation is meaningless without them; (d) cleanup — #56's `destroy` verb, and what happens when it fails; (e) ⚠️ AN EVIDENCE-SURVIVAL CONTRACT, which is load-bearing rather than a detail. It must name what survives a run as evidence: environment facts, tool and runtime VERSIONS, inputs, outputs, exit status, timing, permission denials, and explicit redaction or omission reasons. A MISSING FACT MUST REMAIN VISIBLY UNKNOWN. #96's environmentMatch treats an absent fact as `unknown` rather than `mismatch`, which caps confidence below environment-matched — so a silently omitted fact DECIDES APPLICABILITY WITHOUT ANY READER KNOWING IT HAPPENED. Recording why a fact is absent is what keeps that visible, and it is the difference between 'we did not observe this' and 'this was not observable'. Consequence to decide with the schema: evidence may need a declared place for omissions and redactions, since today an omitted fact and a fact that was never relevant are indistinguishable on the record. Only after those does 'which tier first, implemented how' become answerable.
